Implements `IEnumModesCallback` -- this IS the callback invoked by DirectDraw's native `EnumDisplayModes` for each supported mode. When the output array (`anIntArray4606`) hasn't been allocated yet it just tallies up how many ints are needed (`anInt4608 += 4`, one 4-tuple per mode); on the second pass (array allocated) it writes width/height/bpp/refreshRate into the next 4 slots. Classic two-pass count-then-fill enumeration pattern, driven by `method1145`.

Runs DirectDraw's `enumDisplayModes` twice through `method1144` (the IEnumModesCallback impl on `this`): first pass with no backing array to count total ints needed, then allocates `anIntArray4606` and re-enumerates to fill it. Returns a flat `IntArray` of (width, height, bitDepth, refreshRate) tuples, one per supported mode. Suspicious: `if (bool != true) anInt4608 = 52` truncates the returned array to the first 52 ints (13 modes) whenever `bool` is false, discarding the rest of the freshly-filled array before returning it -- looks like a 'limited/short list vs full list' toggle, but the truncation happens by overwriting the count used to size the returned array rather than slicing cleanly, so confidence is medium on whether `bool=false` is the common/default path at call sites (no call site was found elsewhere in the repo for this batch).
